newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource ups stake in French SIRIS.
newsitem.headline: Unisource ups stake in French SIRIS.

text.p: Unisource, the telecoms joint venture between Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden, Swiss Telecom PTT and Spain's Telefonica, said on Friday it would purchase Compagnie Generale des Eaux' (CGE) 50.01 percent stake in SIRIS.

Unisource currently holds 49.99 percent in SIRIS, a joint venture which was formed in 1995 between CGE and Unisource to bring out a range of national and international voice and data services to French customers.
No financial details were disclosed on the deal.
Unisource said the decision to exercise its option to buy Generale des Eaux's stake in SIRIS followed the French company's decision to link up with British Telecommunications.
"The change of ownership follows the recent decision of CGE to partner with BT of the U.K," it said.

Generale des Eaux in September named British Telecom as one of the main strategic partners for its Cegetel telecommunications venture. The other two partners are Mannesmann of Germany and the U.S. telecoms company SBC.
